How composition error grows with interface count

One geometry at five sizes — 1, 2, 6, 12 and 24 coupled windows — with the cell, the macro-step, the overlap, the ramp, the viscosity and the disk model all held fixed, so the only thing that moves is the number of interfaces. It measures the program's own most-likely-to-fail criterion, F1, which had never been measured at any size.

the gate

The ladder

Five rungs. Two of them are controls: N = 1 has no interface at all and must return a composed defect of exactly zero, and N = 6 is the wake-array case study, whose array loss must come back at the numbers it was published with or the ladder is measuring the harness rather than the physics.

The growth

Log–log, composed defect against the number of overlapping window pairs. A slope of 1 is linear; the criterion fails only above it. The dashed series is the same measurement with the physics held fixed — one turbine at every size, so every window added sits in near-freestream and the only thing that grows is the cut.

Look at it

The wake array's most transferable finding was that a rendering of the state is a measurement instrument: W98 was smooth, bounded, physically shaped, in the right units, passed every control, and was found by watching an animation beside the referent's. Streamwise velocity, same colour ramp at every size, so a frame's brightness means the same thing throughout.

W58 — which bound was measured

The cut-defect bound has more than one reading and the record never said which. Two of them are reference-free, and they differ in how they aggregate: a max over neighbour pairs against a norm over the whole grid of a cellwise max. The first saturates as the tiling grows and the second does not, so the ratio falls with interface count — whatever the contaminated sets are doing.

Does the rollout survive its own length?

Every number above is one macro-step. This is what happens when the composed system is asked to keep running: each rung marched on from its own developed state beside the monolith, with the assembled field's divergence recorded at every step. The third column is the same classical composition with one global projection added to the composition layer — the operator the framework already prescribes, and the one the checkpoint's column already applies.

Wall time — Claim B's other half

Composition is supposed to cost O(1) integration work per added agent. Milliseconds per macro-step per agent, interleaved across rungs and minimum of six repeats, with the instrument's own reproducibility beside it.
